text: To-morrow I will bring him to the Castle.” The Earl's elbow was resting on the arm of his chair; he put his hand up and shielded his eyes with it. “Well,” he said; “go on. You know I told you not to write to me about the matter, and I know nothing whatever about it. What kind of a lad is he? I don't care about the mother; what sort of a lad is he?” Mr. Havisham drank a little of the glass of port he had poured out for himself, and sat holding it in his hand.
